clue.text: Anyway, they are not announced as first teams!

definitions.meaning: in addition, in any case, used as a sentence adverb

definitions.text: they are not announced as first teams
definitions.meaning: B-sides, the second teams or reverse sides of records, which are never billed first; said aloud they sound like the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a sound pun: B-SIDES (second-string teams, or the flip side of a single) is pronounced like the answer, which is why 'announced' is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words serve as a connective meaning moreover or in any event.

clue.text: A bus is diverted in this African capital

indicators.note: a bus that is diverted takes a different route, so its letters, with A and IS, take a new order

explanation.surface: A bus is rerouted on its way through a West African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bissau is the capital city of Guinea-Bissau, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Way aquatic mammal turns up in an end passage

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: an otter is a river-dwelling mammal

explanation.surface: An otter surfacing along a road at the far end of a channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses OTTER to RETTO in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a stretto is the closing section of a fugue, where entries overlap, so it is a passage near the end.

clue.text: Orange dishes may be cooked in it

definitions.text: Orange dishes may be cooked in it

parts.words: Orange dishes may be cooked in it
parts.note: Orange is the Dutch royal house, so a cooking pot from the Netherlands is a vessel for Orange dishes

explanation.surface: A recipe note about which pot to use for something orange-flavoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange' looks like the fruit or colour; it is the House of Orange, the Dutch royal family, so 'Orange' stands for Dutch and the pot dishes are cooked in is an oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy lidded cast-iron cooking pot is called by this name, and dishes are cooked in it.

clue.text: Learning, chars polish furiously!

indicators.note: doing something furiously is doing it wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Cleaning ladies scrub away furiously at the furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chars' are charwomen, British cleaners, but here the word is just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship is academic learning and knowledge gained by study.

clue.text: It helps one to hear a murder suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters of the phrase are untrustworthy and rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective relying on eavesdropping to catch someone suspected of murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a noun, the person accused, but it is the anagram signal for A MURDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane in the ear vibrates with sound and so lets a person hear.

clue.text: Notice Essexopener getting a run

indicators.note: the opener of a county is its first letter, as the opening batsman goes in first

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A cricket notice about the Essex opening batsman scoring a run.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county with a cricket team; 'opener' takes its first letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: To give ear to something is to pay heed, so the word stands for attention or notice.

clue.text: Girl redhead had love trouble

parts.note: the head of the word red is its first letter

indicators.note: had and love are troubled, stirred up into a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired girl going through a hard time in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' stirs HAD and O into HODA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a woman's given name, so it is a girl in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Does such a salad give one a red tongue?

definitions.text: Does such a salad give one a red tongue?

parts.words: Does such a salad give one a red tongue?
parts.note: a salad of diced vegetables in mayonnaise named after a country, whose language is spoken by Reds, or communists

explanation.surface: Wondering whether beetroot in a salad stains one's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red tongue' suggests a stained tongue; it is the language of the Reds, the Soviet communists, and the salad is the one named after their country.
explanation.definitionFit: The salad of diced vegetables in mayonnaise bears this name, and it is also the main language of the former Soviet Reds.

clue.text: In an abstracted manner take body of musicians one at a time

parts.note: MU is the Musicians' Union, the British trade union for performers
doing things singly is doing them one by one

explanation.surface: An instruction to audition members of an orchestra individually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body of musicians' tempts you to take the middle letters of 'musicians'; it is the Musicians' Union, MU.
explanation.definitionFit: Musing is lost in thought, so acting this way means in a dreamy, preoccupied fashion.

clue.text: Brick on which oarsman rests his feet?

definitions.meaning: in bricklaying, a brick laid lengthways along the wall face

definitions.text: on which oarsman rests his feet
definitions.meaning: the footboard in a rowing boat that the rower braces against

explanation.surface: An oarsman bracing his feet against a brick.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a lengthwise-laid brick and the rowing-boat footrest, besides the more familiar carrying litter.

clue.text: Haven in Samoa's islands

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters in Samoa's islands

explanation.surface: A tourist describing the islands of Samoa as a peaceful refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert, and by extension any refuge or haven.

clue.text: Mahler's third, in the full version

definitions.text: Mahler's third, in the full version

parts.words: Mahler's third, in the full version
parts.note: the third letter of the composer's name, written out in full as a word instead of a single letter

explanation.surface: Praise for the uncut recording of a Mahler symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mahler's third' sounds like his Third Symphony; it is the third letter of MAHLER, H, and 'in the full version' asks for that letter's name spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H, when named as a word, is spelt this way.

clue.text: At work he is expected to turn up the volume

definitions.text: At work he is expected to turn up the volume

parts.words: At work he is expected to turn up the volume
parts.note: turn up the volume means find a requested book, not raise the sound level

explanation.surface: Someone whose job requires making things louder, like a sound engineer or DJ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up the volume' reads as raising the sound; here a volume is a book, and to turn it up is to find it, the job of someone working among library shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who looks after a library is expected to find the books readers ask for.

clue.text: Association of ideas

parts.note: read not as the psychological term but as a group of thinkers who supply ideas

explanation.surface: The psychological term for linking one thought to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Association of ideas' is a phrase from psychology; here an association is a body of people, a panel of experts who supply ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A brains trust is a panel of expert advisers, a body of people formed to generate ideas and answers.

clue.text: Chatty Sloane vicar not put out ?

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or upset, so the letters are disarranged

explanation.surface: A talkative clergyman in Sloane Square who is not bothered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' here signals the anagram, though with 'not' before it the surface reads as an unruffled vicar. A Sloane is a posh young Londoner from around Sloane Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversational describes talk that is informal and sociable, the manner of someone talkative.

clue.text: Preoccupation with hot water source?

definitions.meaning: deep absorption in an activity or subject
an electric heater element in a domestic tank, the British word for this kind of water heater

explanation.surface: Someone obsessed with their boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the electric water heater in a hot water tank is commonly just called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means total absorption in something and also names the electric heater for a household tank.

clue.text: In our time, choice is in fosterage

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks dates in the present era
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: Modern attitudes to choice in fostering children.
explanation.definitionFit: Fosterage is the raising of another's child, and legally taking a child as one's own is a close synonym.

clue.text: Decent Thin Man's remake is rather a let-down

indicators.note: a remake of a film reworks it, so the letters of the title are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A film review: the new version of The Thin Man is passable but disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thin Man is a 1934 detective film; 'remake' signals the anagram of its letters with DECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Disenchantment is disillusion, the feeling of being disappointed by something once admired.

clue.text: Sage in paste-spread?

indicators.note: a spread is mixed and smeared out, so the letters of in paste are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A herb mixed into a sandwich paste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sage' looks like the herb going into the paste; it is the adjective meaning wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means wise, as a sage person is wise.

clue.text: Runner, possibly the favourite

parts.note: not a horse in a race but a candidate who runs for office, maybe the frontrunner

explanation.surface: A horse in a race that might start as favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' and 'favourite' suggest horse racing; the runner is a candidate standing for election or an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for a post or prize, who runs as a candidate.

clue.text: Time when dynamo is out of order?

indicators.note: out of order means broken and also not in sequence, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: When the generator breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' reads as broken, but it signals an anagram of DYNAMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week is a period of time.

clue.text: Trophy at end of season is a cruet-piece

indicators.note: at end of places the trophy word after the season word

parts.note: to season food is to pepper it
a pot is slang for a cup or trophy

explanation.surface: A trophy handed out at the end of the sporting season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' looks like a sporting season; it is the verb, to flavour food.
explanation.definitionFit: A condiment set holds a shaker for the spice ground from peppercorns, one item of the set.

clue.text: Pass into America's middle, without a leader

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: center is the American spelling of centre, a middle

explanation.surface: Travelling into the heart of the United States with no guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America's' points to the US spelling CENTER; 'without a leader' removes its C.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass into a place is to go in.

clue.text: Young groom has capital and nothing more

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
nothing is zero, O, and nothing more is added

explanation.surface: A newly married young man owns a city and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Romeo secretly marries Juliet, so he is a young groom.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo is a young lover who weds Juliet, and the name means a young lover generally.

clue.text: Incompetent writer retired in Italy

indicators.note: in places the reversed writer inside the Italy abbreviation

parts.note: IT is the international abbreviation for Italy

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is something one writes with

explanation.surface: A hopeless author who has retired to Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses PEN to NEP, which goes inside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, unable to do a job properly.

clue.text: A tonic due to be drunk is tipped off…

indicators.note: to be drunk is to be unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone warned that a tonic is about to be drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as consumed, the tonic being drunk; it signals the anagram of A TONIC DUE. The ellipsis runs on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cautioned is to be warned, as someone tipped off is given a warning.

clue.text: Colombian mountain pass

definitions.meaning: .... is an abbreviation for Colombia or Colombian
a low point in a ridge between peaks

explanation.surface: A pass through the Andes in Colombia.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters abbreviate the South American country and also name a dip in a mountain ridge.

clue.text: … character in a bar is unaffected

definitions.meaning: in music, the sign that cancels a sharp or flat, written in a bar of the score

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth regular in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; it is a bar of music, and the character is the symbol that cancels a sharp or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the musical cancelling sign and also means genuine, without affectation.

clue.text: Hides in here in attempt to conceal a queen

indicators.note: to conceal means to hide, so the attempt word wraps round the queen

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Anne was a queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: Someone trying to hide a queen in a hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hides' looks like a verb, concealing; it is the noun, animal skins, which are tanned in this works.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where animal skins are turned into leather.
